prompt: A stopwatch with start, stop, reset and lap buttons. It shows time with hundredths of a second and lists every lap, newest first.
A cooking countdown timer: I pick the number of minutes, press start, and it counts down second by second with a progress bar.
A big digital clock that shows the current time and updates every second, with today's date below it.
Draw a gear with eight teeth that slowly rotates, and a button that pauses and resumes the rotation.
Draw a smiling cartoon face: a round head, two eyes, a nose and a curved mouth. A button changes the mood to sad.
A pie chart of my monthly spending by category that I can edit with sliders, drawn as vector shapes.
A tic-tac-toe game for two players on a 3 by 3 board with a score counter and a New game button.
A small minesweeper game on a 6 by 6 board with a counter of remaining mines.
A memory card matching game: a 4 by 4 board of face-down cards, flip two at a time, count the moves.
A simple calculator with a keypad of digits and the four operations and a display.
Arkanoid game: a paddle moved with buttons, a ball that bounces off walls and bricks, a score and lives.
The classic snake game on a grid, steering with four arrow buttons, the snake moves by itself.
A one-day trip itinerary for Lisbon as a timeline of five stops with times, and a checkbox to mark each stop as done.
A medication history: a timeline of the doses I took today with their times, newest at the bottom.
Track a parcel delivery as a timeline of events from warehouse to doorstep, with the current status highlighted.
A workout planner: a text field for the exercise name, a number input for reps, a slider for effort from 1 to 10, a switch for warm-up included, a picker for the muscle group, and a saved list.
A notes app where I type a note in a text field, save it, and see all notes in a list with a delete button each.
A to-do list with a checkbox for each task, a field to add a task, and a progress bar of how many are done.
A settings screen with switches for notifications, dark mode and sound, and a slider for volume.
An alarm app where I choose the wake-up time, pick the days of the week, and turn each alarm on or off.
A medicine reminder: I enter the name, choose the time of day, and it lists all reminders with their times.
A tip calculator: enter the bill amount, pick the tip percentage with a slider, split between a number of people.
A BMI calculator: enter height and weight as numbers and see the result with a category.
A budget tracker: add expenses with an amount and a category chosen from a list, see the total and a progress bar against the monthly limit.
A habit tracker with a checkbox per habit per day, a streak counter, and a progress bar for the week.
A recipe card for pancakes: a photo from a web address, key facts like prep time and servings, an ingredients checklist and the steps.
A contact profile screen: a photo from a URL, key details like phone, email and city, and an edit field for notes.
A weather card for a city with an icon image from a URL, temperature, and key facts like wind, humidity and pressure.
A flight details screen: departure and arrival with key facts like gate, terminal and seat, and a progress bar of the check-in steps.
A multiple choice quiz: one question at a time, pick one answer from options, score at the end.
A quick poll: a question, choose one of four options, show how many votes each option got as progress bars.
A unit converter: choose the unit from a dropdown, enter the value as a number, and see the converted result.
A long scrolling page of 30 facts about the planets, each with a divider between them.
A pomodoro timer with 25 minute work and 5 minute break phases, a progress ring or bar, and a counter of finished sessions.
A reaction time game: wait for the screen to change, tap as fast as you can, show the time in milliseconds and the best time.
A dice roller: pick how many dice with a slider, roll them, show the values and the sum.
A tap counter with plus and minus buttons and a reset.
A scoreboard for two teams with plus buttons and a reset, showing who leads.
Show a random motivational quote each time I press a button.
A coin flip app that counts heads and tails.
A gratitude journal: write one line each day and see the history of entries.
A plant watering log: pick the plant from a list, record that I watered it, and show days since each was watered.
Flashcards for learning words: show a word, tap to reveal the translation, mark known or unknown, progress bar of the deck.
A metronome: set the tempo in beats per minute with a slider, start and stop, and show a visual beat indicator that pulses.
A sleep log: enter bedtime and wake-up time, and see the hours slept for each night with key facts for the week.
A road trip planner: stops on a timeline with arrival times, total distance and fuel cost as key facts, and a field for the budget.
Draw a simple map of a park with paths, a pond and trees as vector shapes, and tap buttons to highlight places.
An analog clock face with hour, minute and second hands drawn as shapes that move every second.
